changes.comment: Code organization refactor stage 8b (Feishu directory reorganization): (1) R37 - every card the package builds is now Card JSON 2.0 (schema '2.0', elements under body.elements); the pairing approval button uses a direct Card 2.0 callback button; the binding-bound/unbound/team-dissolved notification cards go through the shared card kit, which now takes an explicit forward flag so those three cards keep their prior forwardable behavior unchanged; no other visible text, layout, button, or export name changed. (2) R38 - bind_space/get_space/list_spaces no longer report a generation field and list_bindings no longer reports an origin field, since neither was read by any code, only surfaced verbatim. (3) R38/R41 - a topic-kind binding now persists the message id that first triggered it (root_message_id) when automatic provisioning installed it; a manual bind never sets it but preserves one already on the row. (4) R41 - every outbound send now reads the chat/topic it actually landed in off Feishu's own send response instead of a session-local recent-message guess, fixing a class of reply-lands-in-the-wrong-topic bug once two conversations interleave; a reply with no message_id inside a Collaboration Space chat is refused with an instruction, or redirected to the caller's own bound topic when it has exactly one, instead of silently opening a new topic, for every caller kind; a newly auto-provisioned leader's identity preserves the configured identity and appends the bound chat id, the message id that triggered creation, and guidance to use the current message id or that initial id when replying. (5) Ask-user rounds now read their card's landing off the send response the same way. Card-action dispatch (extension keys, pairing approval, the four ask_user_* actions) resolves through one shared action table instead of two separate hardcoded checks. (6) The nine-file feishu-cot-*.ts layout and feishu-inbound-anchor.ts regroup under cot/ by responsibility - the state machine (adapter.ts), byte-size math (bytes.ts), card-event building (card.ts), recipient/anchor state (recipients.ts), the diagnostic log shape (diagnostics.ts), bounded platform I/O (io.ts), and which in-flight submissions are this session's own (inbound-correlations.ts); no behavior or persisted-format change. (7) feishu-channel.ts and feishu-session-ops.ts fold into session/session.ts, replacing the free-function SessionHandle bag with named collaborators or private methods; a built-in MCP tool call now gets the same post-teardown liveness fence an extension tool call already had. FeishuTeamSubmitter is no longer exported (single-method interface with one call site, replaced by a plain function type). Card-click answering and card-driven delivery (an extension's forward, an ask-user settlement, the pairing-approval click) move to a new session/card-actions.ts collaborator the session constructs and delegates to, rather than living as six more private methods on the session class itself. (8) The session, inbound, outbound, access, ask-user, chain-of-thought, and card files move under directories named for what they own (session/, inbound/, outbound/, access/, ask-user/, cot/, cards/); routing/ and tools/ already existed. Files with a single already-clear owner (feishu-submit.ts, feishu-provisioning.ts, feishu-extensions.ts, feishu-slash-commands.ts, feishu-document-comments.ts, bot.ts, extension.ts, plugin.ts, provider.ts, and others) stay at the package root. No behavior change from the moves themselves. (9) The package's public surface (index.ts, the sole package.json exports target) shrinks to the named plugin entry createFeishuPlugin, plus the compatible default/createFeishuChannelProvider neutral provider entry (without plugin extensions), the full extension contract an implementing plugin needs (FeishuApi/FeishuExtension*/FeishuInstanceApi plus their own transitive types - FeishuCardActionEvent, FeishuCardActionResponse/rawCardActionResponse, FeishuTarget, FeishuToolResult, DREAMUX_ACTION_KEY), and the two names packages/dreamux's own test suite reads as a cross-package consumer (formatFeishuMessageForRuntime, FeishuInboundEvent). Every other name the barrel re-exported previously (FeishuChannelSession and its session types, createFeishuSessionMcp, CHANNEL_REMINDER/FeishuChatSubmission/FeishuInboundDelivery/FeishuSubmission/FeishuSubmitOutcome, the FEISHU_TOOLS/FeishuToolContext/FeishuToolDef/FeishuToolSession tool-registry group, FeishuRouting/FeishuBindingView/FeishuRoutingPlan/FeishuRoutingStore/routingDocumentFilename/FEISHU_ROUTING_DOCUMENT_VERSION/FeishuBindingRecord/FeishuRoutingDocument/FeishuSpaceRecord, chatTarget/describeTarget/targetKey/topicTarget/FeishuTargetKind, createFeishuBot/FeishuBot/CreateBotOptions, DREAMUX_PAIRING_CARD_ACTION/DREAMUX_PAIRING_TOKEN_KEY, buildPairingApprovalCard/buildPairingSuccessCard, loadChatBots/PeerBot/ChatBotsListing, formatFeishuCreateTime/FormatFeishuMessageOptions/FormatFeishuMessageResult/FormattedFeishuAttachment, dreamuxFeishuGate, defaultDispatcherAccessState/DispatcherAccessState, VisibleMessageAnchor, and BUILTIN_FEISHU_PROVIDER_REF) had zero consumers reaching it through the package boundary rather than a relative import inside the package, and is removed; every internal caller already used the concrete module. Old routing documents keep loading unchanged under all of this - the generation/origin/root_message_id shape change is additive/stop-writing only. Not BREAKING.
